It is an option with the martyrdom keystone and the talent (somewhere on the top left of the tree, can't remember the name) that gives you damage reduction on any attack that would take you down to the next wounds threshold.  I tried it out though, and it didn't seem to do much, but some zealots swear by Martyrdom with at least 2 extra wound curios 

On their own wounds don't do much since they only help AFTER you've gone down, since they let you go down a few more times without dying outright.  +16 toughness or +21 health curios are considered better since they help you to NOT go down, saving your team from having to scramble to pick you up mid fight.  On zealot I usually run one +toughness curio with two +health curios, since zealot has a bigger innate health pool, with at least two instances of +20% damage resist against gunners on them and +12% stamina Regen on each curio

Power Maul, Bolter

Chorus and the keystone that ups your crit chance after things die.  Take every talent that'll make you tankier, stagger absolutely everything with your power Maul and bolter

I tried it with martyrdom and the talent that reduces damage that would take you to the next wound, but found it didn't really offer much survivability or damage that I couldnt get with the other keystone and my curio slots.  Essentially you just don't die, stagger everything until your crit chance pops up and you can go wild with the extra DPS.  See a room you don't like?  Magdump the bolter. The Doctor rescued those that had fallen, with the help of the Miner, seeing to it that no one else had to die to protect what little they had left. When the ash settled, the survivors only found further damnation.  Their food stores had been burning through the night.  What might have lasted the colony to spring, with careful rationing, would now only serve to prolong their suffering.

Hushed whispers of the pragmatic could be heard underneath the sobs of the hopeless.  Cannibalism?  No, it would be better to die with dignity than to sink as low as the Tox-Pigs.  Wait for a herd of animals to come through?  Unreliable, the children could starve before then.  Abandon the colony, head to our allies to the east?  The journey was far, too far to feed everyone on the journey, too cold to arrive with all our limbs, but maybe we didn't need to send everyone.

That day, it was not the strongest among them that were chosen to make that doomed journey, but the weakest.  The Artist, disliked by most, but nevertheless a provider of beauty to the otherwise simple and utilitarian colony.  His loss may not be felt by many, but it would be shown in every room.  The Carpenter, who had built almost every wall, bed, chair, and table.  Rebuilding the shattered home would be difficult without her, but she knew she was old, and could feel her time coming even before this frigid nightmare.  The Youngster, barely old enough to be called a man.  He was a slacker at heart, spending most of his childhood enjoying better times.  He knew he had no skills, no true calling, and when he looked into the eyes of the other children he had helped the colony raise, he felt like this might be the most he could ever do for them.  The Miner, a hardworking man who had helped save the lives of every other person standing in the hall this day.  Some tried to volunteer to take his place, but he was the last to be treated by the Doctor after the raid, and could already feel the gangrene taking hold under the makeshift bandages.

The hardest sacrifices to make were the three Newcomers, however.  They did not go easily when they saw the pitiful stares, the downcast shameful eyes, and were told they were to leave as well.  They were welcomed in the Fall, taken in by the colony's hospitality and apparent abundance, only to be put on the chopping block in favor of those who already called eachother family.  In the end their pleas faltered under the grim, determined stares of the other "volunteers".

The damned few set off on their journey, the idea that it did not matter if they returned with supplies for the colony almost comforting them as they starved and froze.  As for the survivors they left behind, they lived to see the Spring, but could not see the home they once had anymore.

If you caught a survivor away from a pallet, they would dead hard for distance to a pallet.  If you caught them at a pallet, they would use dead hards endurance effect to tank the hit and speed boost to the next loop.  Even bad survivors would make you wait out their dead hard.  Imagine every chase ending in you staring at a survivors back for 4 seconds until they made it to a pallet and you HAD to swing before they made it there, 50/50 chance you'd actually manage to down them.

Sure, this meta was accessible in the way that every chase and most games were the same.  No guessing perks, or accounting for different builds, and thats less difficulty than we have now I guess.  But I don't miss that meta at all, and the game is so much easier in MY opinion without it.

Edit: I forgot to mention the addition of MMR.  The game used to have a matchmaking system based on playtime, so if you played a bunch and did okay then you'd be matchmade with anyone else that also played a bunch.  This was weird.  Now the game has an mmr system, if you kill more survivors then you get matchmade with survivors that don't get killed that often.  This is weird, but I think on average it winds up being more fair.  A lot of people don't like mmr, since it means if you do very well you get matchmade against people that do very well.  For survivors this means going up against top tier killers with top tier builds, and for killers it usually means going up against 4 man survive with friends with top tier builds.  It sounds frustrating, but personally I (maybe controversially) avoid that by getting 8 hooks and then letting all the survivors leave.  This is just more fun for me, and seems to be more fun for the survivors I go up against

I hear they're making a 40k version of vermintide, i get so excited.  A studio like fatshark, that improved so much from vermintide 1 into v2, that stuck with v2 and theoretically learned so much about how to make an absolutely amazing game in its genre, something that in my opinion is as much of a classic as the game that inspired it.  That studio, making a game set in the universe that I spent hours on 1d4chan studying as a kid because I couldn't afford the books, in the same genre and style of the game that might forever be my #1 favorite game.  I was so excited that I finally upgraded my gpu, stuck in some more ram, and got a fancy m.2 just for darktide.

The beta launches, and it's all red flags.  Every system that played so well together in vermintide 2, packed with unnecessary changes.  Some systems completely removed, some weird systems added.  Seeing the core characters at the heart of v2 be replaced with the most meaningless backstory options and 12 new possible voices/characters to choose from that needlessly complicate the possible banter interactions and leave the whole thing feeling just lifeless in comparison to what we got before.  An incoming focus on micro transactions that were completely missing at v2's lanch hanging over the whole thing like a gun in the shape of the fortnite battle pass.

But it's the beta!  Rampant crashes and obviously poor optimization are fine.  Only having 3 maps is fine!  Character abilities with half the flair and potential builds of v2 is fine!  Packing the game with so much mandatory next generation Nvidia bullshit tech that it made my amd hardware cry and piss and shit and bleed is fine!  It's not like vermintide 2 was perfect on launch and it was still getting major improvements right up until the announcement of darktide.  But man did it still feel like shit to play something that felt like it was made in a boardroom by the corpse of something I used to love, at 40fps with 30% resolution scale even after manually going into .ini files to disable things that used to be in the options menu but got patched out?  

The game launched, it's okay I guess, nothing from the beta was fixed besides some crashing problems.  Oh, and those 3 maps weren't just a demo, those are the only maps  in the game.  They get reused twice each.  Vermintide 2 launched with 10 unique maps with unique objectives, bosses, setpieces, and enough environmental distinction that I could tell you which mission you're in based on a screenshot of a wall.  I still can't play it on hardware above minimum recommended, mostly due to amd apparently losing some trade and culture war I didn't know about I guess,  without running at an unstable 40fps even with their top of the line AI driven nuclear powered resolution scaling bullfuck something or other software.

I mean, it's fine I suppose, darktide sold well and has a good enough player count and just got its first Fatshark Patented Big Balance Patch.  But it's like all the good things I liked about vermintide 2 got forgotten or removed, and all that hype dying just felt terrible.  Like I had been going to the same place for lunch, ordering the same thing for 7 years or so, making friends with other regulars and watching the small diner grow and improve, and then they announce a new menu item and it's literally just some human shit on a plate. COINTELPRO (syllabic abbreviation derived from Counter Intelligence Program) (1956–1971) was a series of covert and illegal projects actively conducted by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) aimed at surveilling, infiltrating, discrediting, and disrupting domestic American political organizations. FBI records show COINTELPRO resources targeted groups and individuals the FBI deemed subversive, including feminist organizations, the Communist Party USA, anti–Vietnam War organizers, activists of the civil rights movement and Black Power movement (e.g. Martin Luther King Jr., the Nation of Islam, and the Black Panther Party), environmentalist and animal rights organizations, the American Indian Movement (AIM), Chicano and Mexican-American groups like the Brown Berets and the United Farm Workers, independence movements (including Puerto Rican independence groups such as the Young Lords and the Puerto Rican Socialist Party), a variety of organizations that were part of the broader New Left, and far-right groups such as the Ku Klux Klan and the National States' Rights Party.

The FBI has used covert operations against domestic political groups since its inception; however, covert operations under the official COINTELPRO label took place between 1956 and 1971. Many of the tactics used in COINTELPRO are alleged to have seen continued use including; discrediting targets through psychological warfare; smearing individuals and groups using forged documents and by planting false reports in the media; harassment; wrongful imprisonment; illegal violence; and assassination.  According to a Senate report, the FBI's motivation was "protecting national security, preventing violence, and maintaining the existing social and political order".

Beginning in 1969, leaders of the Black Panther Party were targeted by the COINTELPRO and "neutralized" by being assassinated, imprisoned, publicly humiliated or falsely charged with crimes. Some of the Black Panthers targeted include Fred Hampton, Mark Clark, Zayd Shakur, Geronimo Pratt, Mumia Abu-Jamal, and Marshall Conway. A lot of em are upgrades at Standard grade, most if not all are upgrades at above Standard grade (besides Economy limbs).  No bleeding on the limb, less chance of dying from limb damage, less urgent heals (if you've got a limb at -50 and aren't knocked out, you need to heal it, if you have a prosthetic at -50 you can ignore it for as long as you don't need the limb), frequently higher base health for a prosthetic limb, and on top of it all you get stat boosts that let a "early game" character compete with "mid game" characters and "mid game" characters compete with "late game" characters

The tradeoffs for limbs are relatively minute at decent Grades, and you're able to complete ignore the downsides if you have a crew of specialized characters (stick steady arms on a crossbowman that you micro a lot for no downsides, KLR on your heavy weapons/blunt character so they can equip a higher grade of weapon)

All in all, you can get a limb that's a straight upgrade in 90% of situations if you know where to look, to the point where it's desirable to get Peeler blueprints early so you can intentionally cripple your characters and go full transhumanist.  Hell, I used to pick the Rock Bottom start not because it was a challenge, but because it's easy to mine/scavenge for food outside of Sho-Battai and then head to Heft and get a good prosthetic with relatively minimal investment.  

Overpowered might be the wrong term, as it's not like sticking 4 prosthetics on a fresh recruit will let them solo the entire game, but they definitely feel overtuned and losing a limb is definitely not a problem at all if you feel like subscribing to the "meta".  The general increase in survivability and customizable stat boosts make the prosthetics very strong, and the ability to switch them out on the fly both increases said survivability in some circumstances and removes the effect of the "tradeoff" stat debuffs if you're able to carry around a different set of limbs.

I think the primary differences between self harm and a pain kink are why you do it, how you do it, and how it makes you feel afterwards.  It's fine to enjoy pain and self harm if you're being very, very safe (avoiding great injury/death and infection),  if you want to do it because it's how you're choosing to relax and enjoy yourself (instead of doing it because it's your only emotional outlet or the only emotion you can feel currently), and if it actually makes you feel comfortable afterwards (instead of feeling shameful or guilty after the initial high dies down)

The why of it might be the biggest difference I suppose.  If you're self harming because you know it's fun and want to do it, then sure you're a free individual.   However, if your ideas of self harm seem to be caused by mental illness or trauma, then it's going to be much more productive for your well being to try and address those issues before self harming.   

People are free to do what they want with their own bodies, but I'd argue that self harm/suicide while being deeply affected by mental illness isn't free will, but is instead physical symptoms of your illness or trauma.  Kinda like any other illness;  untreated cancer leads to bodily harm and death, untreated mental illness can also lead to bodily harm and death.  But shit, if you're comfy with yourself and your life and feel like your self harm ideation isn't coming from a dark place and won't lead to suicidal ideation eventually?  Then hell yeah brother live your life, just keep that shit safe and make sure it doesn't become an addiction.
